metadata.description: Desktop screening candidates; source reconciliation is not hydrological or mounting validation.
metadata.coordinate_assumption: Source latitude/longitude interpreted as WGS84; no reprojection performed.
method_and_caveats: Method

1. Coverage: the 69 H3 resolution-8 hexagons with ≥1 reported active Helium gateway (data/active_hexes.json from stevensismart/Sensors, retrieved 2026-11-13 17:18 UTC; source api-iot.heliumtools.org).
2. Towns: the 22 municipal boundaries in data/municipalities.geojson (US Census county subdivisions) shown as blue lines on the map.
3. Overlap: each hexagon was sampled on a ~22 m grid and each grid point assigned to the town polygon containing it, giving 109 hexagon∩town overlap areas.

4. Flood-prone: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer (hazards.fema.gov NFHL MapServer layer 28, Flood Hazard Zones) queried for each hexagon. 1% annual-chance zones (SFHA: AE, incl. floodway) = flood-prone; 0.2% zone (shaded X) = lower priority.

5. Site points: within each overlap, FEMA water lines (layer 20) inside the 1% floodplain were densified; one point per named stream (up to 2 per overlap) was placed at the middle of that stream reach. Where no stream line exists (tidal Hudson/Meadowlands areas), the point is the center of the 1% floodplain in the overlap; where only a 0.2% zone exists, the center of that zone.
6. Water-surface info: nearest FEMA cross-section (layer 14) on the same stream with its 1% water-surface elevation (WSEL_REG, ft, NAVD88). Static BFE from the zone polygon where FEMA publishes one.

7. Pluvial (rainfall ponding) points: USGS 3DEP bare-earth elevation (elevation.nationalmap.gov 3DEPElevation ImageServer; 1 m lidar-derived source in this area) was downloaded for each hexagon plus a ~150-200 m buffer, resampled to ~1.7 × 2.2 m cells (0.00002°; 15 hexagons that timed out were run at 0.00003° ≈ 3.3 m, one at 0.00004° ≈ 4.4 m — see 'DEM cell size').

8. A priority-flood depression fill was applied; closed depressions (fill depth ≥ 0.05 m) were delineated and kept if max depth ≥ 0.3 m and ponded area 100–40,000 m². Contributing area = cells whose D8 steepest-descent path ends in the depression. Depressions whose low point is < 30 m from a FEMA stream line were dropped as likely culvert/channel artifacts. Per hexagon∩town, the top 3 (by priority, then storage volume) were kept; duplicates < 40 m apart merged.
9. Pluvial priority: High = depth ≥ 1.0 m and contributing area ≥ 10,000 m²; Medium = depth ≥ 0.5 m and contributing area ≥ 2,500 m²; Low = other qualifying depressions.

10. Flood exposure type: 'Fluvial' = FEMA riverine/tidal floodplain site; 'Pluvial' = terrain low point outside the FEMA 1% floodplain; 'Fluvial + pluvial' = a pluvial low point inside the FEMA 1% floodplain, or a fluvial site with a pluvial low point within 150 m.

11. Addresses: reverse-geocoded with OpenStreetMap Nominatim (nearest address or road). Town column is the Census boundary that contains the point; ZIP/mailing locality can differ near borders (see Notes).
Priority (fluvial sites)
1 - High: point on a named stream inside the FEMA regulatory floodway (riverine, well suited to water-level sensors at bridges/culverts).
2 - Medium: inside the 1% floodplain but not floodway, on an unnamed stream, or in tidal/coastal flats.
3 - Low: only the 0.2% (500-yr) zone is present in the overlap.
Caveats
• 'Active gateway' hexagons reflect third-party reported gateway activity, not measured LoRaWAN RF coverage; verify signal on site.
• Points are desktop screening locations, not surveyed sites. Check right-of-way/ownership, mounting structure (bridge rail, pole), and municipal permission before deployment.
• 43 of the 109 overlaps contain no mapped FEMA flood hazard; most of them now have pluvial low-point sites instead.

• The pluvial analysis is topography-only: it ignores storm-sewer capacity, inlets, and pumping, and a bare-earth DEM can show false depressions where roads cross on culverts or where buildings were removed. Some large depressions on open land are engineered detention basins. Validate against municipal flooding complaints / storm-drain maps before deployment.
• Depression depth is the depth before water spills over the lowest rim — the maximum ponding depth if drainage fails, not an expected depth for a specific storm.
• One coverage hexagon (882a100921fffff, near Wood-Ridge) only touches a town boundary by a sliver and produced no overlap at the 22 m sampling.
• FEMA NFHL effective data for Bergen (DFIRM 34003C) and Passaic counties as served on 2026-11-13.
